title: Thailand International Patient Journey
thesis: On one governed platform, Snowflake turns daily appointment activity from 40 synthetic Thai international patient coordination desks into appointment-integrity KPIs, a 7-day appointment-cancellation risk score per desk, payment guarantee decline rate anomalies and AI answers that cite their sources. All data is aggregate desk-day counts with no patient-level records.

talking_points: 40 coordination desks of a fictional hospital group serve five service lines in Bangkok, Phuket, Chiang Mai, Pattaya and Hua Hin; the cards show issue-free appointment rate, journey issues, cancelled appointments and quoted package value in THB.
Each KPI is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so you can trace it back to desk-day rows.
The issue-type chart separates issues that often end in a cancelled appointment, such as declined payment guarantees, from flight schedule disruptions that are always resolved.
tabs.call_out: Patient journey KPIs you can trace to source rows

transition.line: Which desks need a review first?

talking_points: A Snowflake ML classifier estimates, per desk, the chance of a cancelled appointment in the next 7 days.
Precision and recall come from the most recent labelled days held out of training, shown next to the base rate.
Anomaly detection picks out unusual desk payment guarantee decline rates, and the forecast covers the next 14 days of journey issues for coordinator staffing.
tabs.call_out: ML that is evaluated honestly, next to the data

transition.line: Are desks keeping pre-arrival checklists and documents in order?

talking_points: Pre-arrival checklist audit compliance, desk document coverage and pending documents show where desk controls are slipping.
Plotting checklist audit compliance against cancelled appointments per desk shows where the two move together; that is an association, not a cause.
The action memo proposes three prioritised actions using only the KPI, desk, issue-type and risk rows.
show: Checklist audit compliance and document coverage

tabs.call_out: Draft actions grounded in data, reviewed by a person

transition.line: What happens when a booking hits a problem right now?

talking_points: New appointment booking events arrive in RAW.LIVE_BOOKINGS, either from the simulator or from Amazon Data Firehose through Snowpipe. Events carry a desk ID, an amount and a response time, never patient details.
The alert records each ISSUE event with an SOP hint and the desk risk band, then emails the on-call patient journey analyst.
tabs.call_out: From a live journey issue to a desk case on one platform

talking_points: The Cortex Agent answers metric questions with Cortex Analyst over the semantic view, and procedure questions with Cortex Search over 14 synthetic, administrative journey-issue SOPs.
Every answer shows the SQL it generated and the SOP IDs it cited. The agent gives no clinical advice.
tabs.call_out: Answers in plain language that you can check

transition.line: This is how it fits together.

talking_points: One core supports two builds: Snowflake only, or AWS + Snowflake with Data Firehose, Bedrock, QuickSight and Amazon Q.
All data shown is synthetic and rebuilds the same way from the repo.
tabs.call_out: A governed core with an optional AWS edge
